content:
I am trying to build strength for myself. I am currently 194lbs and 6'3". I have a little sore left shoulder. I want look better build shoulders and back primarily so the dress can fit better and also I play cricket and need strength to be able to bat as an opener and bowler and play shorts. Can you guide me how to build this I can share pictures of my body

[user attached 4 photos of physique]

Looking at your photos — good starting point. At 6'3" and 194 lbs you actually have a lean frame underneath; the midsection fat is the main visual issue, and your back shows decent lat width already. The shoulder soreness is the key constraint to work around.

Q: How many days per week can you train?
Q: What equipment do you have access to?
Q: What's your current activity level?
4 days / Full gym / Already training

Perfect. Here's your plan built around your goals — wider shoulders and back for fit, plus cricket-specific strength for batting power and bowling.

The core split: Push / Pull / Legs / Athletic

Given your sore left shoulder, we'll avoid heavy overhead pressing early and build rotator cuff stability first.

Day 1 — Pull (Back + Biceps) ← your priority
- Cable rows — 4x10
- Lat pulldowns (wide grip) — 4x10
- Single-arm dumbbell rows — 3x12
- Face pulls — 3x15 (also heals the shoulder)
- Rear delt flyes — 3x15
- Bicep curls — 3x12

Day 2 — Push (Chest + Shoulders, shoulder-safe)
- Incline dumbbell press — 4x10
- Lateral raises — 4x15 (the #1 move for wider shoulders)
- Machine chest press — 3x12
- Cable lateral raises — 3x15
- Tricep pushdowns — 3x12
- No overhead barbell press until shoulder feels 100%

Day 3 — Legs + Core
- Squats or leg press — 4x10
- Romanian deadlifts — 3x12 (builds posterior chain for bowling)
- Lunges — 3x10 each leg
- Plank + rotational core work

Day 4 — Athletic (Cricket-focused)
- Deadlifts — 4x6 heavy (batting power comes from here)
- Cable rotations / woodchops — 4x12 each side (direct transfer to batting)
- Farmer's carries — 3x40m
- Band pull-aparts — 3x20 (shoulder rehab)
- Medicine ball rotational throws if available

For the shoulder: Add 5 minutes of band pull-aparts and external rotations before every session. Face pulls 3x per week minimum. Avoid pain — if lateral raises hurt, do them with cables seated instead.

For body composition: At 6'3"/194 lbs you're not far off — the goal is recomposition, not a big cut. Aim for 180-190g protein daily (roughly 1g per lb bodyweight). Don't eat in a big deficit or you'll stall muscle gain.

Want me to build this into a weekly tracker or go deeper on the cricket-specific strength side?
something like this not very bulky
Can you share the reference image you have in mind? It looks like you meant to attach a photo but it didn't come through!
[reference image of lean athletic physique attached]

Great reference. This is actually very achievable for your frame — it's not bodybuilder bulk, it's athletic lean. The key features here are:
- Round, capped shoulders (lateral delt width)
- V-taper back (lats flaring out)
- Lean midsection — visible but not shredded abs
- Full chest without being massive

The good news: At 6'3" and 194 lbs, you already have the height advantage. This guy is probably sitting around 10-12% body fat. You're likely around 20-22%. So your job is two things simultaneously — lose ~15-20 lbs of fat while building the shoulders and back.

What this means for your plan: The training I outlined is already correct. The missing piece is nutrition, because you can't reveal this physique without losing the midsection fat.

Calorie target: ~2,400-2,500 kcal/day (slight deficit, preserves muscle)
Protein: 180-190g daily — non-negotiable
Timeline: Realistically 9-12 months of consistent work

The three moves that build exactly this look:
1. Lateral raises — every single week, heavy volume
2. Pull-ups / lat pulldowns — builds that V-taper
3. Face pulls — rounds out the rear delt for that 3D shoulder look

You have great genetics for this — tall frame means the V-taper will look dramatic once the fat comes off. Want a simple meal framework to hit the protein targets without overcomplicating it?
I cannot do pull ups or push ups

No problem — your shoulder is likely the issue with push-ups too. Here's how we replace them:

Pull-up replacements (same muscle, no bodyweight strain):
- Lat pulldowns — identical movement pattern, you control the weight
- Assisted pull-up machine if your gym has one
- Cable straight-arm pulldowns — great lat isolator

Push-up replacements:
- Machine chest press — zero shoulder stress
- Incline dumbbell press — you control the angle to avoid pain
- Cable chest flyes — very shoulder-friendly

Revised plan reality check: Everything I gave you still works — pull-ups and push-ups were never in the program. The gym machines and cables are actually better for building the aesthetic you want because you can isolate more precisely.

The shoulder soreness — is it more painful with pressing movements (pushing forward)? Overhead movements (lifting above head)? Lateral movements (raising arm to side)?

This matters because lateral raises are the #1 exercise for that capped shoulder look, and I want to make sure we find a version that doesn't aggravate it. Some people do fine with cable lateral raises even when dumbbell ones hurt.
when I sat i cannot means I have never been able to maybe we will have to build that strength

Ah that makes total sense — at 6'3" bodyweight movements are genuinely harder, you're moving a lot of weight. Pull-ups are one of the hardest exercises for taller guys.

Good news: you don't need them at all to get that physique. The gym machines will get you there faster honestly.

For pull-ups specifically — if you ever want to work toward them, the path is:
1. Lat pulldowns get your back strong enough
2. Assisted pull-up machine builds the pattern
3. Negatives (jump up, lower yourself slowly) build the final strength

But that's optional. The reference physique is 100% buildable without a single pull-up.

One thing I want to flag — given you're already training, what does your current gym routine look like? Because the most common mistake people make is too much chest/biceps, not enough back and shoulders, wrong rep ranges for the aesthetic goal.

If you share what you're currently doing, I can tell you exactly what to swap or add rather than starting from scratch.

yeah my current workout schedule s focused on upperbody with inclined bench press normal bench press seated pulls seated shoulder exercises and biceps

bench press i can do 20lbs 3 sets 10-12 reps
shoulder 15lbs same sets
seated pulls 79lbs same sets
biceps 15lbs 3 sets 15-20 reps

Good baseline to work from. A few observations:

What's working: Seated pulls at 79 lbs is solid — your back has a head start. That's good news for the V-taper.

What's missing for your goal:
- No lateral raises (the single most important move for capped shoulders)
- No rear delt work (critical for that 3D shoulder look)
- No deadlifts or rows (back thickness)
- Legs completely absent — this matters for cricket and also for testosterone/overall muscle building

The weight reality: 20 lbs on bench and 15 lbs on shoulders is quite light for your frame. You're likely in "maintenance" mode, not growth mode. To build muscle you need progressive overload — adding weight or reps consistently every 1-2 weeks.

Here's what I'd tweak immediately without overhauling everything:
1. Add lateral raises — start at 10 lbs, focus on form
2. Add face pulls — 30-40 lbs cable
3. Bump bench toward 30-35 lbs dumbbells
4. Add one leg day — even just squats and Romanian deadlifts

How long have you been on your current routine? And are you seeing any progress or has it plateaued?
20 lbs each hand same 15 lbs each hand

That changes things significantly! So you're actually at:
- Bench: 40 lbs total per rep (each hand) — decent starting point
- Shoulders: 30 lbs total — respectable given the sore shoulder
- Biceps: 30 lbs total

That's a much better foundation than I thought. You're not a beginner — you're an intermediate lifter who just needs redirection toward the right muscles.

The main gap is still: No lateral raises, no rear delts, no pulling variety (only seated pulls), no legs.

Your immediate next steps are simple. Add these three exercises to what you're already doing:
1. Lateral raises — you can probably start at 12-15 lbs each hand. This is the shoulder width builder.
2. Face pulls on cable machine — rear delt and shoulder health
3. Romanian deadlifts — 40-50 lbs dumbbells — back thickness + cricket power

Don't overhaul everything at once. Just plug these in and within 6-8 weeks you'll see visible shoulder width change.

Progressive overload target for next 3 months:
- Bench → 35 lbs each hand
- Lateral raises → 20 lbs each hand
- Seated pulls → 100 lbs

Want me to write this out as a clean 4-day schedule you can screenshot and take to the gym?
yes

Here you go — clean and ready to screenshot:

ANIKET'S 4-DAY GYM PLAN
Goal: Athletic V-taper + Cricket strength

- Lat pulldowns wide grip: 4x10-12, 60 lbs

DAY 2 — SHOULDERS (Tuesday)

- Lateral raises: 4x15, 12 lbs each

DAY 3 — REST (Wednesday) Walk 20-30 mins. Light stretching.

DAY 4 — CHEST + TRICEPS (Thursday)
- Incline dumbbell press: 4x10-12, 20 lbs each
- Flat bench dumbbell press: 3x10-12, 20 lbs each
- Cable chest flyes: 3x12, 20 lbs
- Tricep pushdowns: 3x12, 30 lbs
- Overhead tricep extension: 3x12, 20 lbs

DAY 5 — LEGS + CORE (Friday)
- Goblet squats: 4x12, 30 lbs
- Romanian deadlifts: 4x12, 40 lbs each
- Leg press: 3x12, 100 lbs
- Cable woodchops: 3x12 each, 20 lbs
- Plank: 3x45 sec

DAY 6 & 7 — REST

Progressive Overload Rule: Every 2 weeks, add 5 lbs to each exercise if you can complete all reps cleanly.

3-Month Targets:
- Seated rows → 100 lbs
- Lateral raises → 20 lbs each
- Incline press → 30 lbs each

Daily Nutrition: Calories ~2,400, Protein 180g minimum, Water 3-4 liters

Shoulder Rule: Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain. Face pulls every session — they heal the shoulder over time.

Screenshot this and take it to the gym. Want a simple high-protein meal plan to go alongside this?
[image attached] is this rear delt fly

Yes, exactly! That's the bent-over rear delt fly — great exercise and it's in your plan.

Key form points from that image:
- Hinge forward at hips ~45 degrees
- Slight bend in elbows (not straight arms)
- Raise dumbbells out to the sides like wings
- Squeeze at the top, lower slowly
- Keep your back flat, don't round it

One thing to note — this standing bent-over version requires some lower back stability. Since you're building up, I'd recommend starting with the seated version instead: Sit at the edge of a bench, lean your chest onto your thighs, and do the same fly motion. Much easier to control and same muscle activation.

Start at 8-10 lbs each hand — this muscle is small and most people go too heavy and use their traps instead. Light weight, slow and controlled is the key here.

This is honestly one of the best moves for that 3D rounded shoulder look in your reference photo. Do it every back day and shoulder day.
this is good qq i have is how will i get 180-190g protein daily i am a south indian eating eggs chicken and mutton goat mostly i try to do my dinner by 6;30 can you guide me with some options

Perfect — eggs, chicken and mutton are actually ideal for hitting protein targets. South Indian food works really well for this.

Here's a simple daily structure:

Breakfast (7-8am) — ~50g protein
- 4 whole eggs + 2 egg whites scrambled — 30g
- 100g chicken (leftover from previous night works) — 25g
- Or eggs with a small portion of idli/dosa

Mid-morning snack (11am) — ~30g protein
- Greek yogurt (Chobani plain) — 17g
- Handful of roasted peanuts or almonds — 8g
- Or 2 boiled eggs — 12g

Lunch (1-2pm) — ~50g protein
- 150-200g chicken curry — 40-45g
- Small portion rice — energy for training
- Dal on the side adds another 8-10g

Pre/post workout snack (4pm) — ~30g protein
- 3 boiled eggs — 18g
- Or whey protein shake — 25g in one shot

Dinner by 6:30pm — ~40g protein
- 150-200g mutton/goat curry — 35-40g
- Vegetables, small rice portion

The honest shortcut: A whey protein shake once a day fills gaps easily — one scoop is 25g protein and takes 30 seconds. Given your dinner cutoff at 6:30, it's very useful post-workout.

Total: ~200g protein — right in target.

Want me to suggest specific Indian-friendly protein sources ranked by value?
yes

Here's your ranked list — all easy to find and fit South Indian cooking:

TIER 1 — Best bang for protein
- Chicken breast: 31g per 100g, cheapest per gram
- Egg whites: 11g per egg, nearly zero fat
- Whole eggs: 6g per egg, best overall food
- Mutton/Goat: 25g per 100g, higher fat but great protein
- Tuna (canned): 30g per 100g, easiest quick meal

TIER 2 — Good supporting proteins
- Greek yogurt: 10g per 100g, easy snack
- Paneer: 18g per 100g, good if you eat dairy
- Chana/Chickpeas: 9g per 100g, great in curries
- Moong dal: 7g per 100g, light and easy to digest
- Rajma: 9g per 100g, good with rice

TIER 3 — Supplementary
- Whey protein: 25g per scoop, fastest gap filler
- Peanuts: 26g per 100g, easy snack
- Milk: 8g per cup, easy to add

Practical South Indian combos that hit protein hard:
- Egg curry + rice: 35g easily
- Chicken biryani (protein forward portion): 40-45g
- Mutton curry + roti: 40g
- Egg dosa (2 eggs inside): 20g
- Boiled eggs as snack

The simplest rule: Every single meal should have a fist-sized portion of chicken, eggs, or mutton. If it does, you'll hit 180g without counting calories obsessively.

The one supplement worth adding is whey — just once a day post workout.
I cannot have egg chicken and mutton everyday

Totally understandable — eating the same things daily gets old fast. Here's how to rotate and keep it interesting:

Add these to your rotation:
- Fish — if you eat it, incredible protein. Salmon, tilapia, rohu, katla all work great in South Indian curries
- Prawns/Shrimp — 24g per 100g, cooks fast, very South Indian friendly
- Canned tuna — mix with onion, green chili, lemon — done in 2 mins, 30g protein

On days you go lighter on meat:
- Paneer — bhurji, curry, tikka — very filling, 18g per 100g
- Chana — chole, sundal, chana curry — easy 20-25g per meal
- Moong dal + rice — comfort food, add ghee, solid protein
- Rajma — rajma rice is a complete meal
- Greek yogurt — as a side with any meal adds 15-20g effortlessly

Realistic weekly rhythm:
Monday: Chicken
Tuesday: Eggs + Dal
Wednesday: Fish or Prawns
Thursday: Mutton
Friday: Paneer + Chana
Saturday: Chicken
Sunday: Whatever you enjoy

The whey shake becomes more important on vegetarian days — it's your safety net to hit targets without forcing meat every day.

What days do you typically go meat-free?
my first day can you give me the schedule

How does this feel — is the gym near your home or office? Trying to understand when you'd typically go so we can align this with your 6:30 dinner cutoff.
session 2

DAY 2 — SHOULDERS
Rest 60-90 seconds between sets

1. Seated Dumbbell Press — 4 sets x 10-12 reps, 15 lbs each hand
Press straight up, don't lock elbows at top, lower slowly to ear level

2. Lateral Raises (Dumbbell) — 4 sets x 15 reps, 12 lbs each hand
Slight bend in elbow, raise to shoulder height only, pinky slightly higher than thumb, lower slowly — this is your most important exercise

3. Cable Lateral Raises — 3 sets x 15 reps each side, 10 lbs
Single arm, cable at ankle height, raise across body to shoulder level, slow and controlled

4. Face Pulls (Cable) — 3 sets x 15 reps, 30 lbs
Every shoulder day without fail — heals and builds simultaneously

Same as Day 1 — rear delts need frequency to grow

Total time: ~40-45 mins

Shoulder check: If the dumbbell press causes sharp pain, drop to 10 lbs and reduce range of motion. Never push through sharp pain — dull burn is fine, sharp pain is not.

Before you start: 5 mins light lateral raises with 5 lbs just to warm the shoulder joint up gently

How did Day 1 feel? Any exercises that felt awkward or caused discomfort?
should I also add running and rowing?

Good instinct. Here's the honest answer:

Running — yes, but strategically
For your goals it serves two purposes — fat loss and cricket fitness (you need to run between wickets and field). But don't overdo it while building muscle.

Recommended:
- 2-3 times per week, 20-30 mins
- Not on the same day as legs — your legs need recovery
- Best slots: Wednesday and Saturday (your rest days)
- Moderate pace — not sprinting, not slow walk

Rowing machine — absolutely yes
This is actually perfect for you specifically because:
- Builds back and lats directly (supports your V-taper goal)
- Great shoulder-friendly cardio
- Mimics cricket movements
- Burns fat while building muscle simultaneously

Add 10 mins rowing as a warmup before every back day. It primes the exact muscles you're about to train.

Updated weekly structure:
Monday: Back + 10 min rowing warmup
Tuesday: Shoulders
Wednesday: 20-30 min easy run
Thursday: Chest + Triceps
Friday: Legs + Core
Saturday: 20-30 min run or cricket
Sunday: Full rest

This keeps cardio from eating into muscle recovery while still burning fat consistently. Given your 6:30 dinner cutoff, when do you typically train — morning or evening?
morning

Perfect — morning training actually works best for your schedule. Here's how to structure your mornings:

Ideal Morning Flow
- 6:00am — Wake up
- 6:15am — Pre-workout snack (optional)
- 6:30am — Gym
- 7:15-7:30am — Done, whey shake immediately
- 8:00am — Proper breakfast

Pre-workout on empty stomach? Two schools of thought — honestly for your goals either works. But if you feel weak or dizzy training fasted, have one of these 15 mins before: 1 banana, 2 dates, small handful of peanuts. All quick energy without sitting heavy in your stomach.

The morning advantage for you specifically:
- Done before the day gets busy with SurveyMonkey and Statis work
- Metabolism elevated all day
- Dinner at 6:30 is perfect — 8-9 hours after training, muscles fully fed by then
- No evening willpower needed

One thing to protect: Sleep. Morning training only works if you're getting 7-8 hours. If you're up late building Statis, the gym will suffer. Recovery happens during sleep — it's as important as the workout itself.

What time do you usually wake up currently?
cable is fixed with minimum as 40 lbs

Good to know — here's how to adjust:

Face pulls at 40 lbs — actually fine, just focus on slow controlled reps. Don't let the weight pull you forward.

Cable lateral raises at 40 lbs — this is too heavy to start, the lateral delt is a small muscle. Two options:
1. Skip cable laterals for now — just do dumbbell lateral raises instead, you have full control over weight there
2. Use the cable but with a rope attachment — sometimes the angle makes 40 lbs more manageable

Revised Day 2 shoulders with this fix:
- Seated dumbbell press: 4x10-12, 15 lbs each
- Dumbbell lateral raises: 4x15, 12 lbs each
- Extra set lateral raises: 2x20, 8 lbs each
- Face pulls: 3x15, 40 lbs
- Rear delt fly seated: 3x15, 10 lbs each

So you replace cable laterals with an extra dumbbell lateral raise set. More volume on the most important shoulder exercise — actually better for your goal.

Does your gym have adjustable cable machines or is it all fixed stack?
face pulls seems to be easy with 40

That's a good sign — it means your rear delts have some base strength already from your seated pulls.

Progressive options for face pulls:
- Move to 50 lbs and see if you can still do 15 clean reps
- If yes, go to 60 lbs
- The sweet spot is where rep 13-14-15 feel genuinely hard but form doesn't break

Form check at heavier weight — common mistakes:
- Shrugging shoulders up (traps taking over — bad)
- Leaning back too much to pull the weight
- Elbows dropping below shoulder level
- Rushing the rep

The cue that fixes everything: Pull to your nose, elbows stay high and wide, pause 1 second at your face, then slow 3-count return. If you can do that cleanly at 60 lbs for 15 reps you're doing great.

Honest target progression:
- This week: 50 lbs
- Week 3-4: 60 lbs
- Week 6-8: 70 lbs
- Month 3: 80+ lbs

Test 50 lbs tomorrow on Day 2 and see how it feels. What weight are you currently doing seated cable rows at — still 79 lbs or have you gone heavier?
I am able to do 120 lbs for face pulls

That's impressive — your rear delts are genuinely strong, probably from years of cricket bowling and batting movements.

So face pulls for you:
- Start at 120 lbs, aim for clean 15 reps
- Progress to 140 lbs when 15 reps feel easy
- This is actually great news — strong rear delts means your shoulder has good stability underneath, which explains why it hasn't gotten worse

This changes how I think about your shoulder: The soreness is likely not weakness — it's probably one of these:
- Rotator cuff irritation from repetitive bowling motion
- Front delt overuse from bench pressing without enough rear delt balance
- Poor shoulder mobility rather than strength issue

The fact that you can face pull 120 lbs suggests the muscles are there — it's the joint mobility and balance that needs work.

Add this 3 min routine before every session:
- Arm circles — 30 seconds each direction
- Cross body shoulder stretch — 30 seconds each side
- Doorway chest stretch — 30 seconds
- Band or light cable pull aparts — 20 reps

This will reduce the soreness significantly within 2-3 weeks.

Updated strength picture of you:
- Seated rows: 79 lbs — Good
- Face pulls: 120 lbs — Strong
- Bench press: 20 lbs each — Building
- Shoulders: 15 lbs each — Building

Your back is ahead of your push muscles — which is actually ideal for the V-taper goal. Keep it that way.
day 3

DAY 3 — REST + RECOVERY
This day is as important as the gym days

Morning — 20-30 min easy run
- Comfortable conversational pace
- Not sprinting — you should be able to talk while running
- This burns fat without touching muscle recovery
- Great for cricket fitness — building your running base for between wickets

Shoulder mobility routine (10 mins):
- Arm circles forward: 30 seconds
- Arm circles backward: 30 seconds
- Cross body shoulder stretch: 30 sec each side
- Doorway chest stretch: 30 seconds
- Neck rolls: 30 seconds
- Light band pull aparts: 20 reps

Nutrition focus today: Since you're not lifting, some people undereat on rest days — don't. Your muscles are actually rebuilding today.
- Keep protein at 180g+ — same as training days
- Slightly lower carbs if you want — skip the pre workout banana
- Hydration is critical — 3-4 liters

Mental recovery too: You're running SurveyMonkey work, building Statis, family with Anusha — rest days are for the mind too. Don't feel guilty about not being in the gym.

Ready for Day 4 — Chest and Triceps?
can I add biceps today

Yes absolutely — it's a rest day from heavy lifting so light bicep work fits perfectly. They're a small muscle that recovers fast.

Add this after your run:

Bicep finisher — 20 mins
- Dumbbell curl: 3 sets x 12 reps, 15 lbs each
- Hammer curl: 3 sets x 12 reps, 15 lbs each
- Concentration curl: 3 sets x 15 reps, 12 lbs each

Why these three:
- Dumbbell curl — standard bicep builder
- Hammer curl — builds the brachialis, makes arm look thicker from all angles
- Concentration curl — isolates the peak, gives that round bicep look

Form tip for all three:
- Don't swing your body to lift the weight
- Slow 3-count on the way down — this is where biceps actually grow
- Squeeze hard at the top for 1 second

Updated Day 3:
- Morning: 20-30 min run
- Post run: Shoulder mobility 10 mins
- Then: Bicep finisher 20 mins
- Rest of day: Recovery, eat well

At 15 lbs each hand your biceps are already decent. You'll likely move to 20 lbs within 4-6 weeks. Ready for Day 4?
what else can i do i am not sore

Good — not being sore on a rest day is actually normal and fine, soreness isn't the measure of a good workout. But if you have energy, here's what you can add without hurting recovery:

Option 1 — Forearm work. Great for cricket — grip strength for batting and catching in slips
- Wrist curls: 3x20
- Reverse wrist curls: 3x20
- Farmer's carry: 3x40m walk

Option 2 — Core work. Direct transfer to bowling power and batting rotation
- Plank: 3x45 seconds
- Dead bug: 3x12 each side
- Cable woodchops: 3x15 each side

Option 3 — Rowing machine. 20 mins easy pace — active recovery, burns fat, doesn't tax muscles

Honest advice though Aniket: The temptation when you feel good is to do more. But muscle growth happens during rest not during training. If you genuinely feel fresh, it likely means you're recovering well, nutrition is good, sleep is adequate. That's a good sign — don't punish it by overtraining. The gains will show up. Ready for Day 4?
